# OpenType and legacy kerning controls

Original controls generated by `tools/opentype_kerning_fixture.py`; no corpus
text, artwork or font binaries are included in the DOCX files. The scaffold is
the project's original exhausted-cell-indents fixture. The reference application exported these references read-only. PDFs contain the reference application's subsets of
installed fonts for reference rendering, following the existing reference policy.

Each file has 32 right-aligned 12 pt paragraphs: eight strings each in Goudy Old
Style, Times New Roman, Arial and Calibri. Every run requests kerning at 1 pt
and standard/contextual ligatures. Only `enableOpenTypeFeatures` differs (0/1);
both settings parts have the required relationship and content-type override.
The w14 extension is declared ignorable through MCE. Both packages pass the
standard schema view (six XML checks); this does not prove rendering agreement.

`reference.json` records source/PDF hashes and extracted text positions.
Regenerate it with `tools/record_opentype_kerning.py` after fresh reference exports.
With OpenType enabled, Goudy's mixed digits start 1.80 pt farther left, repeated
ones 7.80 pt farther left, the letter sample 4.92 pt farther left, and the phone
sample 1.44 pt farther left. The other three fonts have identical positions in
these samples. The wider Goudy lines are consistent with the reference application omitting its
legacy kern pairs; the installed font has a kern table and no GPOS/GSUB table.
That explanation is an inference, not a universal rule proved by four fonts.

The renderer now omits legacy-only kerning when enabled OpenType ligatures
select that path and explicit character spacing is zero. The original controls
are passing native-position and
edit/export/undo regressions. Local metadata must be authorized and consistent
across the requested family's faces; unknown or mixed families keep their
previous behavior.

Earlier scratch probes had an unreferenced settings part and are superseded.
Without the ligature declaration, toggling the setting did not change Goudy's
measured positions; this is not a digits-only rule. Font capabilities determine
the correction, without family-name exceptions or number-specific offsets.

References: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.19 (kern),
[MS-DOCX §2.3.3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/116847ff-9af6-45a7-a21f-0e0ff2eef41d).
The MS-DOCX extension describes enabling OpenType behavior, default off; it does
not specify this exact interaction with a legacy-only kern table. Do not call
the observed interaction a demonstrated contradiction of the standard.

## Eight-font follow-up

`tools/legacy_kerning_fixture.py` authors `legacy-0.docx` and `legacy-1.docx`:
48 right-aligned lines each, contrasting none/standardContextual ligatures with
three strings in eight fonts. `tools/record_legacy_kerning.py` binds their native
native reference PDFs and extracted positions in `legacy-reference.json`.

Goudy Old Style, Garamond, Bell MT and Bodoni MT have legacy kern tables without
GPOS and reproduce the omitted-pair behavior with enabled ligatures. Palatino,
Constantia and Arial have GPOS; Book Antiqua has neither table. All 48 enabled
lines match within 0.2pt after correction. The disabled Palatino letter sample
exposes a separate existing GPOS-versus-legacy selection difference (1.2pt
between reference settings). It remains an explicit expected failure, not a relaxed
passing oracle. Other disabled rows and both original four-font controls pass.

The subsequent `../legacy-kerning-pairs` control isolates this further: four
disabled Palatino strings, including an internal-space pair, fail while all
enabled lines and the other three families pass. Simply removing GPOS also
breaks Constantia's legacy-table handling. A private legacy-pair-to-GPOS
prototype matches all 56 disabled native positions, but still needs selective
lookup replacement to preserve mark and other script positioning. This remains
an unresolved production feature, with strict expected failures retained.

`legacy-spacing-positive.docx` and `legacy-spacing-negative.docx` repeat the
48 enabled cases with +0.3pt and -0.3pt character spacing. The reference application retains legacy
kerning for both spacing signs, even with standardContextual ligatures enabled.
`spacing-reference.json` binds these references. Their native PDF encodes
hyphens with dummy zero origins; those are excluded from line-origin extraction
and identified in the recorder rather than claimed as valid glyph coordinates.
These controls prevent the correction from widening tracked text while fixing
untracked text in the same document.

The correction uses a private in-memory FontFace with its kern table removed,
retaining glyphs, hinting, metrics and substitutions. Merely setting Canvas
fontKerning to none was rejected: Cyrillic glyphs falling back to Noto Sans
lose their own GPOS kerning. A regression checks those fallback pairs. Original
font bytes never change and no derived font is stored, exported or uploaded.
Synthetic-bold advances use a correspondingly derived single-weight face.

Local Font Access can group condensed and ordinary subfamilies together. Face
registration retains the requested family's width, normal/italic styles and
weights. The installed Bell MT also contains a non-Macintosh cmap language of
1, which browser font validation rejects. The derived face normalizes that
metadata field to 0, as required by the OpenType cmap specification, without
changing character-to-glyph entries; Macintosh language fields are retained.
Independent SFNT controls test that normalization and checksums. This is a font
metadata repair, not evidence that the reference application contradicts a DOCX clause.

Re-export the four new native PDFs read-only with `tools/export-reference.ps1`
after regeneration, then run the recorder, `tests/opentype-kerning.test.js`,
`tests/browser/opentype-kerning.spec.js` and DOCX schema validation. Font bytes
are acquired only from already-authorized Local Font Access, for document
families that request the feature. Preparation is cached; ordinary text and
font-picker listings do not trigger this work.

Font metadata references: [OpenType OS/2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/os2),
[OpenType cmap language fields](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/cmap#use-of-the-language-field-in-cmap-subtables).
